messages:
Maria Chen: Heads up — per-shard queue depth is spiking on eu-west-2 shard-pool-7. Mosaic-XL requests piling up, ~2500 queued, p95 latency > 4s. Can someone triage?
Ajay Patel: looking... are these from a single customer or across models?
Maria Chen: mostly mosaic-xl traffic + a few rerank jobs. KV cache miss rate jumped to 72% on pool-7.
Lina Gómez: logs show lots of small requests that kill batching. sample:
```json
{
  "shard": "pool-7",
  "model": "mosaic-xl",
  "queued": 2531,
  "in_flight": 48
}
```
Kevin Wu: suspect routing fallback created a hot shard. Autoscaler didn't add nodes because pod CPU was low — looks IO bound (nvme/ephemeral).
Ajay Patel: suggest temporary admission-control: reduce per-route `max_in_flight` to 32 for mosaic-xl in eu-west-2, and enable spill-routing to us-west-2 for non-SLA traffic.
Maria Chen: agree. Ops, can you flip the spill routing and set rate limit?
oncall-ops: I can do a quick change — planning to set route config: `spill_threshold=1200`, `spill_target=us-west-2`, `route_mode=best_effort`, and `per_route_max_in_flight=32`. Will patch in ~2m.
Kevin Wu: watch cost — spilling to us-west-2 will add egress and cross-region GPU usage. Quick estimate: ~$1.8k/hr if sustained at current QPS.
Lina Gómez: also propose increasing `batching.window_ms` to 40ms to improve packing for small requests. That should raise batching_efficiency and lower per-token cost.
Ajay Patel: can we do a canary: change only for shard-pool-7 and traffic tagged `customer:non-enterprise`?
oncall-ops: doing canary now on pool-7 for non-enterprise.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: routing-change rollout started for `config/routing/eu-west-2/spill-2022` — canary=pool-7/non-enterprise.
Maria Chen: after change, queue dropped to ~900 within 30s. p95 down to 2.1s.
Kevin Wu: good. keep monitoring; file follow-up to investigate cache warmup and why IO throttled autoscaler. If miss rate stays high we should consider pinning hot models to dedicated pools or enabling per-customer reserved slots.
Ajay Patel: I'll open a ticket for model pinning + cost analysis and link telemetry graphs.
Lina Gómez: note for postmortem: examine why autoscaler didn't react — agent metric for nvme/io_saturation wasn't wired into scaling policy.
oncall-ops: noted, rolling canary forward; will roll back to stable in 15m if regressions appear.
Maria Chen: thanks team, nice quick run. :thumbsup:
